LuxC-related packaged fixtures were each inspected: (1) pyhmmer/tests/data/hmms/txt/LuxC.hmm — full scientific answer for the LuxC.hmm endpoint (model body byte-identical to the exported output after HMMER version/DATE/COM provenance lines; verified by direct diff after the first controlled run); declared for removal and the removal was validated in a fresh passing reference test (controller receipt files_removed=1, excluded_files_absent=true). (2) pyhmmer/tests/data/msa/LuxC.sto and seqs/LuxC.faa — byte-identical copies of the required scientific inputs, which the analysis legitimately reads from the staged /inputs copies; left in place since removal is not required for offline execution (the source reads its own staged inputs). (3) pyhmmer/tests/data/msa/LuxC.hmmalign.sto — a Stockholm alignment output of hmmalign with no scores/E-values/domtbl fields; it does not represent either exported endpoint and was not removed. (4) LuxC.weighted.sto, LuxC.sto.ssi, msa/LuxC.faa (different, 5993-byte file) — different-input fixtures, not answer exposures. The packaged tables/ directory contains only PF02826, RREFam, bmyD and A0A089QRB9 tables, none for LuxC, so no domtbl answer is bundled. No package-code references to tests/data exist in runtime modules, so the removal does not affect the analysis. Remaining uncertainty: the catalog review targeted LuxC-named and test/example assets from the two installed distributions; it is not an exhaustive semantic audit of every package file.
explanation: The pyhmmer "Build a profile HMM from an alignment and search protein sequences" notebook runs to completion offline. Inputs were staged from the pyhmmer repository at the notebook's pinned source revision (data/msa/LuxC.sto, sha256 e2cf20e9…, Stockholm 1.0 with #=GF ID LuxC, 12 sequences; data/seqs/LuxC.faa, sha256 7ce47aa…, 12 unaligned LuxC proteins; matching the relative paths and revision the example uses). Environment: pyhmmer==0.12.3 (the version of the pinned source revision) with its psutil dependency, installed via uv from wheels on Python 3.13.13; no system packages needed. The controller-executed offline reference completed with exit code 0, produced both reviewed endpoints in /work/outputs — LuxC.hmm (187,150 bytes; model body identical across runs, differing only in DATE/COM provenance lines) and LuxC.domtbl (4,093 bytes, sha256 fc3da85a…, identical across both controlled runs, indicating reproducible hit scores and E-values) — and both declared input files remained byte-identical after execution. The printed top-hit alignment executed as in the source. A packaged full answer (pyhmmer/tests/data/hmms/txt/LuxC.hmm) was identified by diff against the exported endpoint and declared as a dependency exclusion, and a fresh reference test with the removal applied completed successfully.
source_adaptations: Two input-path literals in analysis.py were changed from relative notebook paths to the persistent staged-input paths: pyhmmer.easel.MSAFile("data/msa/LuxC.sto") → "/inputs/data/msa/LuxC.sto" and pyhmmer.easel.SequenceFile("data/seqs/LuxC.faa") → "/inputs/data/seqs/LuxC.faa". The bytes read are identical (sha256-verified against the pyhmmer repository at the notebook's pinned revision 90d2f28); only the file location differs, because the controller recreates the run directory and the original relative paths would not resolve. No other statement, algorithm, parameter or output was changed.
unresolved_assumptions: The LuxC data files were sourced from the pyhmmer repository's packaged test data at the pinned revision (the docs/examples directory contains no copy of its own); their sha256 checksums are pinned and verified in the staging recipe. This is the same lineage the documented example uses, given the notebook imports only pyhmmer and references these exact relative paths.

pyhmmer 0.12.3 was selected because it is the version declared by the source revision's pyproject.toml on the checked-out commit; it installed as a wheel (no source build needed) and is presumed binary-compatible with the tested HMMER behavior on CPython 3.13.13.

The exported LuxC.hmm is byte-reproducible except for provenance lines (HMMER version, DATE, COM command), which is inherent to the HMMER3 ASCII format; the model body was observed identical across both controlled runs.
